items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: But I hadn’t even heard of Charlie Parker when I went down there

ctx.x: When you were at North Texas State, I’m going to jump around a little bit, but I’ve got that on my mind. How much of the — I don’t know if you can give me a percentage — but how much of what you learned there turned out to be useful in the real world of a gigging, working musician?

Well in that I was basically about one step removed from a blank slate when I went down there, you know as a self-taught rock & roll guitar player, so I had just started to get into different jazz guitar players when I went down there. Joe Pass and Grant Green, guys like that, of course Wes. But I hadn’t even heard of Charlie Parker when I went down there, and I was, when was that, so I was 22.
